The real problem is selective summarization: a one-line canon annotation presents the conservative within-RCT figure as the paper's bottom line while omitting the authors' stated ~15% estimate. corrected_finding.problem: The annotation pairs the 31% overall incidence with '8% attributable to drug' — which is the paper's within-RCT antidepressant-placebo summary difference (0.08, 95% CI 0.04-0.12) — while omitting the authors' own stated conclusion that, accounting for non-specific (nocebo) effects seen in placebo groups (17%), discontinuation-symptom incidence is approximately 15%, about one in six to seven patients. Presenting only the lower figure as 'attributable' mis-summarises the paper's bottom line and could lead residents to under-counsel patients stopping or switching antidepressants; both figures come from the same abstract and a canon annotation should not silently pick the lower one.
corrected_finding.replacement: 31% incidence (vs 17% after placebo); authors estimate ~15% attributable (one in six to seven patients), though the within-RCT drug-placebo difference was 8%
corrected_finding.basis: Henssler J, et al. Lancet Psychiatry 2024;11(7):526-535 (abstract verified via PubMed, doi:10.1016/S2215-0366(24)00133-0): incidence of at least one discontinuation symptom 0.31 (95% CI 0.27-0.35) after antidepressant vs 0.17 (0.14-0.21) after placebo discontinuation; within-RCT summary difference 0.08 (0.04-0.12); severe symptoms 0.028; authors' interpretation: 'the incidence of antidepressant discontinuation symptoms is approximately 15%, affecting one in six to seven patients.'
